name: 06-096 CMR Chapter 570, Combined Sewer Overflow Abatement (DEP rule)
access_detail: Word .doc from the Secretary of State rules page, linked from the DEP CSO page; converted with textutil (raw/ch570.txt).
cadence: Annual CSO progress report and 'CSO Activity and Volumes' form for the previous calendar year (Ch. 570 s.6-7); permits set the due date as March 1.
legal_basis: 06-096 CMR Ch. 570; authority 38 M.R.S. s.341-D and s.464(2-B). Effective March 14, 1975; repealed and replaced February 5, 2000.
status_reason: Primary legal basis. It requires public notice of CSO impacts, but only as an annual newspaper notice, permanent signs and direct letters; there is no per-event deadline.
notes: Key text, s.3(B)(3)(b): 'a minimum notification program must consist of: (i) Timely annual publication of prominent notices in newspapers having general circulation in the area affected by CSO discharges; (ii) Posting of permanent signs, where feasible, at locations that afford public access to water affected by CSO discharges such as parks and boat launches; and (iii) Direct written contact with persons known to have particular interest in the use of land or waters affected by CSO discharges.' 'All notices must include a description of the area and uses impacted by CSO discharges, the nature, times and conditions of impacts, and precautions that should be observed by the public.' Nine minimum controls s.5(H): 'Public notification to ensure adequate knowledge of CSO occurrences and CSO impacts.' s.6 data: 'precipitation from storm events or snow melt flows that cause CSOs, overflow volumes and overflow events for the period of January 1 to December 31 of each year'.

name: 38 M.R.S. s.464(2-B) CSO subcategories and s.464(3)(C) report on status of licensed discharges
access_detail: Fetched statute page (curl, browser UA).
status_reason: Statutory basis for CSO subcategory notice and the biennial status-of-discharges report; no event notification.
notes: s.464(2-B)(C)(6): 'In a manner prescribed by the board, applicants receiving approval of CSO subcategories shall provide notice to the public in the area affected, describing the limitations on use of the water body.' s.464(3)(C): 'During the first regular session of each Legislature, the commissioner shall submit to the joint standing committee ... a report on the status of licensed discharges.' The annual CSO Status Report itself is not required by statute (it is filed under DEP 'legislative reports' and described as informing permittees and the public). 38 M.R.S. s.466 defines 'Combined sewer overflow'.

name: 38 M.R.S. s.414-D Municipal satellite collection systems: unauthorized discharge reporting
cadence: Oral report to DEP within 24 hours of becoming aware; written report on DEP form within 5 days.
status_reason: Only statutory SSO reporting deadline found; reports go to DEP, not the public.
notes: s.414-D(3)(A): 'An initial report of the unauthorized discharge must be provided orally to the department by the owner or operator of the system within 24 hours of the time the owner or operator becomes aware of the discharge.' (B): 'A written report ... within 5 days ... must contain ... the cause of the discharge, the date and time of the discharge, the location of the discharge, information on any water bodies that may be impacted by the discharge, the number of gallons of wastewater discharged'. No public notice requirement.

name: 06-096 CMR Ch. 523 Waste Discharge License Conditions / MEPDES Standard Conditions (24-hour reporting of bypasses and SSOs)

cadence: Oral within 24 hours; written within 5 days; to DEP only.
legal_basis: 06-096 CMR Ch. 523; MEPDES Standard Conditions D(1)(f) 'Twenty-four hour reporting' (revised July 1, 2002)
status_reason: Defines when DEP must hear about an SSO or bypass; no public notice.
notes: Permit text: 'The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment. Any information shall be provided orally within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances. A written submission shall also be provided within 5 days'. DEP form instructions add: 'any unanticipated bypass which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit [including sanitary sewer overflows (SSO's) and dry weather overflows (DWO's) from CSO discharge points]'. Anticipated bypass: 'prior notice, if possible at least ten days before the date of the bypass.'

name: MEPDES CSO permit special conditions (signs, nine minimum controls, annual reporting)
access_detail: Read Hampden ME0102512 final 2026, Cape Elizabeth ME0102806 draft 2026, Skowhegan ME0100625 final 2026 (EPA Region 1 posts Maine DEP permits). Text in raw/.
status_reason: Confirms Maine CSO permits carry no event-based public notification condition; only signs and an annual NMC 'public notification' report item.
notes: Hampden 2026 Special Condition 10 'Signs': 'the permittee must install and maintain an identification sign at each CSO location as notification to the public that intermittent discharges of untreated sanitary wastewater occur ... minimum of 12" x 18" in size with white lettering against a green background'. Annual report item (8): 'Public notification to ensure that the public receives adequate notification of CSO occurrences and CSO impacts.' Same wording in the Cape Elizabeth 2026 draft.

name: Scan of CSO permittee websites for overflow notices (23 sites)
access_detail: Homepages of LACWA, Bangor, GAUD, Saco, Biddeford, Bath, South Portland, Westbrook, Lewiston, Auburn SD, Brewer, Skowhegan, Gardiner, Calais, Belfast, Old Town, Orono, Machias, Bar Harbor, Rockland, Winslow, Madawaska, Cape Elizabeth scanned for links containing overflow/CSO/alert/notification. Several did not respond or returned 403 (Bath, Auburn SD, Old Town, Machias, Madawaska: no response; Gardiner, Belfast: 403).
status_reason: No permittee publishes CSO event notices on its homepage; general municipal alert systems (CivicAlerts, AlertSense 'Notify Brewer', enotify) carry no CSO category.
